This is a correct and non-trivial account of the cause of hallucination -- it's not just a surface analogy, since the analogy is explicitly mapped onto the model's actual behavior rather than left as a loose comparison. Requiring specific jargon (next-token probabilities, statistical language modeling) as a condition for full credit was too strict, since the rubric's underlying concept -- that models produce plausible-sounding text without a built-in truth-verification process -- is clearly and correctly conveyed. The mitigation strategy (retrieval/grounding before answering) is clearly stated and correctly tied back to addressing the identified cause. Taken together, both required components of the question are adequately and correctly addressed, meriting full credit rather than partial credit.
